description: Verify that DUT drops a gratuitous ARP Response carrying an unknown hw_type and, on the next UDP egress to that IP, emits its own ARP Request to resolve fresh — proves the bad announcement was rejected, not silently learned
approach:
[Objective]
A two-phase observation. Phase 1 confirms DUT does not learn from a malformed gratuitous ARP. Phase 2 forces DUT to send something to the same IP — if DUT had wrongly learned, it would reuse the injected MAC; if DUT correctly dropped, it must resolve via its own ARP Request.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester → DUT: gratuitous ARP Response injected
   • opcode      = 2
   • hw_type     = some unknown value   ← bad
   • sender_ip   = HOST-1-IP
   • sender_mac  = MAC-ADDR1
   • target_ip   = HOST-1-IP

2. Tester → DUT: SOME/IP SubscribeEventgroup
   ⇒ stimulates DUT to send a UDP response to HOST-1-IP.

3. Observation (5 s window):
   • DUT → broadcast: ARP Request asking for HOST-1-IP   ← key: cache was NOT poisoned by step 1
   • DUT's UDP, when it arrives, must NOT carry MAC-ADDR1 as eth_dst (that would mean step 1 was learned)

[Pass condition]
DUT emits its own ARP Request for HOST-1-IP and does not use MAC-ADDR1 in the UDP egress.

[Fail condition]
• Fail_udp_used_injected_mac — DUT's UDP carried MAC-ADDR1 as eth_dst → DUT silently learned the malformed announcement
• Fail_no_dut_arp_request — DUT did not emit its own ARP Request → it neither learned nor resolved (incomplete reception path)

verdicts.Pass: DUT dropped the malformed gratuitous and resolved via its own Request — normal
verdicts.Fail_udp_used_injected_mac: DUT used MAC-ADDR1 in UDP — silently learned a malformed announcement
verdicts.Fail_no_dut_arp_request: DUT did not resolve via its own Request — reception path incomplete
